alt://instagram.ftlv23-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/731808419_17869706940626857_5699204675989796243_n.heic|As we celebrate Independence Day, I want to share the story behind our National Anthem. Many of us know the words to The Star-Spangled Banner, but fewer know the incredible story that inspired them. In September 1814, during the War of 1812, Francis Scott Key boarded a British ship under a flag of truce to negotiate the release of an American prisoner. After the negotiations were successful, the British would not allow Key to leave because he had learned details of their upcoming attack. He was held under guard aboard a ship in Baltimore Harbor and forced to watch as the British unleashed a relentless bombardment on Fort McHenry throughout the night. Hour after hour, rockets lit the sky and cannon fire shook the harbor. Through the darkness, smoke, and explosions, no one knew if the fort had survived. Then, as dawn broke and the smoke began to clear, Key looked toward the fort. "O say, can you see, by the dawn's early light..." He wasn't simply asking if he could see a flag. He was asking whether America had survived. When he saw the Stars and Stripes still flying over Fort McHenry, he knew the defenders had held their ground. The flag had become proof that freedom had endured another night."...gave proof through the night that our flag was still there." Those words remind us that our flag has never represented comfort or convenience. It represents courage in the face of uncertainty, sacrifice in the defense of liberty, and hope that refuses to disappear even in the darkest moments. As we celebrate the Fourth of July with family, friends, and fireworks, let's remember that our Independence was won through tremendous sacrifice, and our freedoms have been preserved by generations of brave Americans ever since. May we never take those freedoms for granted. Happy Independence Day. Mike Michna Candidate for Texas House District 134
